newsitem.title: USA: Calif. San Onofre 1,080 MW nuke restart delayed.
newsitem.headline: Calif. San Onofre 1,080 MW nuke restart delayed.

text.p: Restart of the 1,080 megawatt (MW) unit 3 at the San Onofre nuclear power plant in San Clemente, Calif., has been delayed until Sunday night, a spokesman for the plant said Thursday.
The unit was scheduled to reconnect with the power grid Thursday, but the delay was caused by work to drain the unit's lube oil system, which has some water contamination.
Unit 3, which has been shut since mid-April for refueling and maintenance, is expected to take several days to reach full power after it reconnects to the grid.
Meanwhile, San Onofre's 1,070 MW unit 2 was holding at 70 percent power while maintenance work on one of its two main feedwater pumps was carried out, the spokesman noted.
Southern California Edison Co, the plant's operator, had no estimate for how long unit 2 would remain at 70 percent power.
Unit 2, which reconnected with the regional power grid early Wednesday, was shut in late June for unplanned repairs.
